sessions.title: This Year's Sessions
sessions.subtitle: Twelve sessions on problems met in production and how they were solved.

lazyRow.title: This UI? LazyRow Won't Cut It
lazyRow.speaker: Yeojun Yoon
lazyRow.summary:
A field report on building a 3D carousel in Compose that LazyRow simply could not handle.

Covers driving every frame with zero recomposition, fixing misaligned touch targets on 3D-transformed UI, and running Paging3 on a screen without a Lazy list.

crashToPr.title: From Crash Triage to AI-Authored PRs
crashToPr.speaker: Pilju Bae
crashToPr.summary:
Collects user entry paths through Firebase and BigQuery, then analyses crashes automatically with an in-house code-aware LLM.

A build log of the pipeline that turns the cause and the fix into a GitHub Actions draft PR.

aiQa.title: Surviving the QA Flood with AI
aiQa.speaker: Dongmin Park
aiQa.summary:
From MCP versus CLI to personas and sub-agents, ending with AI driving the emulator directly to run QA.

Shares the process that runs from self-QA through to the fix, along with the results it produced.

workflowAx.title: Workflow AX in Practice — From Policy Automation to E2E
workflowAx.speaker: Raemin Kang · Dayeon Baek
workflowAx.summary:
Shapes the workflow with a harness and holds AI to the team's conventions through a custom convention gate.

Covers organising policy automatically with an LLM wiki and building a verification process with unit tests, E2E and Roborazzi — with measured results.

webviewLoading.title: Cutting WebView Load Time for Slow Networks and Low-End Devices
webviewLoading.speaker: Kimun Kim
webviewLoading.summary:
Examines why WebView creation cost and rendering optimisations hit a wall on low-end devices and slow networks.

Walks through intercepting requests natively and ultimately running a local web server inside the app.

a2ui.title: Android A2UI: Safe AI-Driven UI Rendering on Jetpack Compose
a2ui.speaker: Jaichang Park
a2ui.summary:
Introduces A2UI, a declarative protocol that lets AI agents render UI safely.

Builds a Compose renderer from scratch, covering state mapping and streaming responses, and compares it with SDUI and Remote Compose.

haptic.title: Introducing Jindong, a Declarative Haptics Library
haptic.speaker: Hyunwoo Lee
haptic.summary:
Haptics remain one of the hardest things to express declaratively.

Introduces Jindong, a haptics library for Compose Multiplatform, and looks at expressing patterns through a DSL and wiring state and lifecycle through the Compose runtime.

overseasCareer.title: Working Abroad as an Android Developer
overseasCareer.speaker: Jaewoong Eum
overseasCareer.summary:
Five years of working at companies outside Korea.

Covers the overseas job market as an Android developer sees it, the interview process, work culture, fully remote setups and business travel.

No experience level or prior knowledge required.

baseline.title: Delegating Migration and Refactoring Safely with Baselines
baseline.speaker: Seongyong An
baseline.summary:
AI made library updates and refactoring easier, but changes to the manifest or resources only surface after release.

Uses baselines to catch unintended changes up front and sets a standard for judging the direction of AI-generated code.

biometric.title: Engineering Biometric UX Across Android Versions
biometric.speaker: Bunjiro Miyoshi
biometric.summary:
Traces the biometric APIs from FingerprintManager to BiometricPrompt and the OS and OEM differences Jetpack Biometric cannot hide.

Looks at how enrollment changes, lockout, cancellation and Keystore invalidation should shape user flows.

audioPlugin.title: Building Audio Plugin Ecosystem for Android in 2026
audioPlugin.speaker: Atsushi Enomoto
audioPlugin.summary:
Android has no common audio plugin format at the platform level, so we have to build one ourselves.

Discusses the technical options available and how the ecosystem has been built up so far.

resumeFeedback.title: Resume Feedback
resumeFeedback.speaker: Organizers
resumeFeedback.summary:
Resume Feedback is a session where the DroidKnights organizers review your resume and portfolio live, on the spot.

After two years as a side programme — and the strongest response of any — it moves to the main track this year.

The selected resume goes up on screen and the feedback happens with the audience watching. Sharp and direct, but always aimed at growth.

For anyone who keeps rewriting their resume without knowing what is wrong, who struggles to put their career into words, or who is ready to take unfiltered feedback head-on.

Three people are selected, and the ticket they paid for is refunded (goods excluded). Tickets may sell out, so buy yours first.

Applications close on Monday 12 October 2026 at 23:59 KST, and results are sent individually by email.
